> **Stacked on #48376 (1/N).** This branch includes #48376's commits; the change to review here is the commits after `d7ac615487` ([compare](https://github.com/esarafian/sglang/compare/qsa-kv-host-offload-store...qsa-kv-host-offload-fused)). I will rebase once #48376 merges.

## Motivation

#48376 (1/N) added host offload of the QSA K/V for Qwen4-Exp. It keeps the full-attention K/V in pinned host memory and a per-request GPU cache of the selected blocks, and it works with the radix cache. Its resolve (selected positions → GPU rows, swapping missing blocks in from the host) is an eager torch reference with host synchronizations, so it needs `--disable-cuda-graph` and costs about 63 ms per decode step at 61K-token contexts on a 300 W RTX PRO 6000 (measured in PR 1/N).

This PR adds a fused Triton resolve that keeps every table on the GPU and needs no host synchronization, so decode and target verify run inside CUDA graphs. It is the default on CUDA.

**Series.** Stacked on PR 1/N and must merge after it. On its own merits it replaces the eager resolve with a CUDA-graph-safe one; it adds no other feature.

## Modifications

- **`mem_cache/qsa_kv_offload_kernels.py` (new):**
  - `_resolve_kernel`: one program per request. It does the tail-ring bookkeeping, takes the unique selected blocks, keeps an exact per-request LRU (double-buffered order list), and refreshes stale blocks: a block is reused only while `req_to_token` still maps its positions to the slots it was filled from. It also writes the copy plan and the per-column device rows.
  - `_copy_plan_kernel` and `_ring_load_kernel` read the planned host rows through their pinned UVA addresses. `_write_through_kernel` copies new rows to the host.
  - Requests past `num_real` (CUDA-graph padding) are skipped.
  - A complete block leaving the tail ring is not copied into the LRU from its ring rows. The backend stores the new token before the resolve runs, so those rows may already be overwritten. The block is loaded from the host on its next miss instead: at most one 4-token block per request and layer every 4 decode tokens.
  - A selected column that resolves to no device row should not happen. It is counted on the device and raises at the next eager forward (an async pinned copy, no host sync), so attention never silently skips a token.
- **`mem_cache/qsa_kv_offload.py`:**
  - The fused resolve is the default on CUDA (not HIP: it reads the host store through raw UVA pointers). `SGLANG_ENABLE_QSA_KV_OFFLOAD_TORCH_RESOLVE=1` selects the eager reference (A/B, debugging).
  - Under the fused resolve the torch tables are not allocated.
  - The verify mode's checks accumulate on the device, so they also run inside CUDA graphs, and leave out CUDA-graph padding rows, which the resolve gives no device row (`real_rows`). In verify mode the offload reads one snapshot of `req_to_token` per forward (`snapshot_mapping`), so its resolve and the full-pool reference read the same mapping even when the scheduler rewrites it mid-forward. They are read back on every eager forward (one host read of two counters, in verify mode only) and at shutdown; any mismatch raises, and progress is logged at most every 10 s. Serving itself reads the live table; a mapping rewritten mid-forward is handled there by the resolve's staleness check, not by the verify mode.
- **`layers/attention/qwen_sparse_attn_backend.py`:** binds the offload at graph capture and sets `num_real` on every eager forward and graph replay.
- **`arg_groups/qsa_kv_offload_hook.py`:** decode CUDA graphs are allowed. Prefill CUDA graphs stay off, because the prefill context gather is built from host-side lengths.
- **Tests:** `test_qsa_kv_offload.py` runs both resolves and adds a CUDA-graph test: the resolve captured once and replayed with new positions, new `req_to_token`, radix remaps and padded requests. Padded rows must be -1 and leave every table unchanged. PR 1/N's backend-level test `test_qsa_kv_offload_backend.py` (offload on vs off through `QwenSparseAttnBackend`, bitwise) runs with both resolves.
- **Docs:** `environment_variables.mdx` row for the torch-resolve switch, and a Qwen3.8-Flash-Next cookbook section: when to use the offload, the launch line, host and GPU costs, and incompatible features.

## Accuracy Tests

The offload stays bit-exact.

- **Unit tests** (`test/registered/kernels/ops/attention/qsa/test_qsa_kv_offload.py`): for both resolves (fused and torch) × BF16, FP8→BF16 and FP8→FP8 packing × decode and 4-row verify, the packed decode scratch from the offload's row table is bit-identical to upstream's gather through `req_to_token` on the full pool. The scenarios include eviction at the minimum hot-cache size, radix remaps and verify rejections. The fused error counter stays 0. **13 pass**, plus PR 1/N's backend-level test with both resolves (2 pass).
- **End to end, inside CUDA graphs:** `SGLANG_DEBUG_QSA_KV_OFFLOAD_VERIFY=1` with decode CUDA graphs on, the same 24-request mix as PR 1/N, H = 512 blocks, RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Server Edition (600 W). At this PR's head, **15 runs, 0 mismatches** (27,552-29,544 checks each; 4 of them with every decode batch size 1-8 captured). Earlier commits passed too: ≥ 24,516 checks on an RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell (300 W) and 29,448 at 600 W.
  - Two verify false positives were found and fixed while gating; serving output was not affected by either.
  - **CUDA-graph padding.** A decode batch padded to the next captured size (3 requests in the size-4 graph) reported mismatches in every padded step. The resolve leaves padding rows unattended by design, but the verify reference still gathered them. The reference now leaves them out.
  - **Mapping rewritten mid-forward.** About one run in eight reported 2 differing tensors, i.e. K and V of one check. The diagnosed case was one decode row of 4, in the first QSA layer only, with 280 of 2,050 columns differing, at prompt positions (e.g. 20,268 of 20,370) during the shared-prefix concurrent phase. Mechanism (code): the scheduler rewrites a running request's `req_to_token` rows (radix dedup in `RadixCache.checkpoint`) on its own stream while the next forward runs. The old and new rows point at K/V of the same tokens, so attention is equally valid with either, as it is on `main`. But the resolve and the reference could read different rows within one layer. Verify mode now copies the mapping once per forward, and both read that copy; serving still reads the live table.
- **Token identity vs `main` on GB200, inside CUDA graphs**, where deterministic inference runs for this model: one GB200, TP1, `--enable-deterministic-inference --attention-backend flashinfer`, decode CUDA graphs on (`--disable-prefill-cuda-graph`), offload on with in-server verify, the same 24 requests. **24/24 outputs are token-identical** to `main` with the same arguments; verify ran 27,900 checks with 0 mismatches.
- Token identity vs `main` is not gated on SM120, for the reasons in PR 1/N: `main` is not run-to-run deterministic for this model there, and deterministic mode needs more shared memory than SM120 has.
- **gsm8k** (`sgl-eval run gsm8k --num-examples 200 --temperature 0 --max-tokens 4096`). Serving args as in the speed test, with `--context-length 20480` and decode CUDA graphs on. Hardware: RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Server Edition (600 W).

  | Run | Offload off | Offload on |
  |---|---|---|
  | `main` vs this PR, separate allocations | 97.5% | 96.5% |
  | this PR off then on, one allocation | 97.5% | 96.0% |
  | this PR off, on, off, one allocation | 96.0% / 96.5% | 97.0% |

  The spread is run-to-run noise. In the off-on-off run, the two **offload-off** runs produce different text for 194 of 200 questions, and off vs on differ on 188-192. Correctness changes on 2-3 questions in every pair. Mean: 96.9% off vs 96.5% on (± 1.2 pp standard error per run).

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Setup: `main` and this PR on the same GPU and image; decode CUDA graphs on and `--disable-prefill-cuda-graph` on both sides.
- Common args: `--tp 1 --quantization modelopt_fp4 --mem-fraction-static 0.93 --max-running-requests 32 --chunked-prefill-size 4096 --context-length 65536`.
- This PR adds `--enable-qsa-kv-offload --qsa-kv-offload-host-size 60 --qsa-kv-offload-hot-blocks 1024`.
- Load: `python3 -m sglang.benchmark.serving --backend sglang --dataset-name random-ids --random-input-len 61440 --random-output-len 1024 --random-range-ratio 1.0 --num-prompts 16 --max-concurrency 16`, three runs per arm (seeds 1-3) on one server. Shown as median [min-max].

**RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Server Edition (600 W)**, this PR's resolve as reviewed (commit `a7751467da`):

| Arm | KV tokens | Max running | Output tok/s | Median TTFT | Median TPOT | Duration |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `main` | 308,416 | 4 (KV-bound) | 139.5 [126.5-145.3] | 44.8 s [36.3-58.1] | 15.3 ms [15.3-17.2] | 117.4 s |
| this PR | 2,441,280 | 11 (GDN-state cap) | **165.1** [148.0-177.8] | 39.5 s [39.4-46.7] | 23.6 ms [22.8-24.4] | 99.2 s |

- **Output throughput +18%**, and the ranges do not overlap. With 61K-token sessions the offload runs 2.75× the concurrent sessions (4 → 11) at the default GDN-state budget.
- The fused resolve costs about 8 ms per decode step at 11 running vs `main` at 4 (TPOT 23.6 vs 15.3 ms), against about 63 ms for PR 1/N's eager resolve.
- Prefill gathers the whole context from the host for every chunk after the first. A follow-up could gather only the rows the top-k reads.

**RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell (300 W)**, same args and load, at earlier commits of this PR (`0f7be68f88`, `eb5e54a7e5`), before the review changes to the resolve and PR 1/N's sizing change; the sizing of both rows is the same at the final head:

| Arm | KV tokens | Max running | Output tok/s | Median TTFT | Median TPOT | Duration |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `main` | 306,624 | 4 (KV-bound) | 126.9 [114.9-132.7] | 48.8 s [44.4-67.0] | 16.4 ms [15.5-18.6] | 129.1 s |
| this PR | 2,441,280 | 11 (GDN-state cap) | **143.8** [133.5-161.4] | 55.3 s [44.4-58.1] | 21.3 ms [20.6-29.8] | 114.0 s |

- Output throughput +13%, though the ranges only just separate.
- Single runs, not claimed (same setup, 256 output tokens): 61K × 24 prompts, `main` 42.8 tok/s with 4 running vs this PR 41.8 tok/s with 11 running (this load is prefill-bound); 16K × 48 prompts, `main` 127.2 vs this PR 123.0 tok/s, both at 11 running.
- In-server verify gate wall time, same 24 requests: 72.9 s with this PR's resolve vs 190.6-201.1 s with PR 1/N's eager resolve. Not a serving benchmark.

- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

+### 2.3 Long Context on One GPU: QSA K/V Host Offload
+
+Qwen3.8-Flash-Next decodes with QSA sparse attention: each query reads at most 2,048 of its context's tokens per QSA layer, but every token's full-attention K/V normally stays in GPU memory. In long-context, many-session deployments that K/V, not compute, caps the number of concurrent requests. `--enable-qsa-kv-offload` keeps the full-attention K/V in pinned host memory and keeps on the GPU, per request, only a cache of the blocks the indexer selects. The output is unchanged (bit-exact), and the radix cache keeps working.
+
+```bash
+sglang serve --model-path nvidia/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-NVFP4 --quantization modelopt_fp4 \
+  --enable-qsa-kv-offload --qsa-kv-offload-host-size 60 --qsa-kv-offload-hot-blocks 1024 \
+  --max-running-requests 32 --disable-prefill-cuda-graph
+```
+
+- **Host memory:** `--qsa-kv-offload-host-size` GB per TP rank, pinned. The logical KV pool is the smaller of what the GPU and the host allow; each token costs the full K/V bytes on the host. This store comes on top of other pinned host memory, in particular the PLE n-gram embedding table, which this model offloads to pinned host memory by default (`--ple-offload-embedding`). Size the host store so that both fit in host RAM.
+- **GPU memory:** per logical token only the QSA index and any MTP draft pool. Per request slot, `(hot_blocks + 2) × compress_ratio` K/V rows per QSA layer (about 0.1 GB at 1,024 blocks with a BF16 KV cache), plus one extend scratch.
+- **What limits concurrency next:** the GDN (Mamba) state cache. Give it the freed GPU memory with `--max-mamba-cache-size`.
+- **Not combinable with:** HiCache, HiSparse, LMCache, PD disaggregation, DP attention, context or pipeline parallelism, mixed chunked prefill, n-gram or tree speculation (`--speculative-eagle-topk` > 1), or prefill CUDA graphs. Decode CUDA graphs and chain MTP speculation are supported.

+"""QSA sparse attention over the K/V host offload (``--enable-qsa-kv-offload``).
+
+Under the offload, the device K/V pool of the QSA layers holds only the hot-cache
+and scratch rows of ``mem_cache/qsa_kv_offload.py``. These functions are the
+backend's offload paths: store the new K/V into device rows and through to the
+host, gather a prefill's cached context from the host, and run decode / target
+verify attention through the offload's per-forward device-row table. In the
+debug verify mode the full pool stays on the GPU and every offloaded read is
+compared with the full pool's.
+"""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+from functools import partial
+from typing import Tuple
+
+import msgspec
+import torch
+
+from sglang.srt.layers.attention.qsa.sparse_attn import (
+    pack_qsa_prefill_kv,
+    qwen_sparse_kv_extraction_compact_triton,
+    qwen_sparse_valid_counts_triton,
+)
+
+
+class QSAKVGatherSource(msgspec.Struct, frozen=True):
+    """Where sparse attention reads K/V: row ``i``, column ``j`` reads
+    ``k_buffer[slot_table[row_requests[i], indices[i, j]]]`` for
+    ``0 <= indices[i, j] < sequence_lengths[i]``."""
+
+    k_buffer: torch.Tensor
+    v_buffer: torch.Tensor
+    slot_table: torch.Tensor
+    row_requests: torch.Tensor
+    sequence_lengths: torch.Tensor
+
+
+def _pack_gathered_kv(source: QSAKVGatherSource, indices: torch.Tensor):
+    """(valid counts, packed K, packed V) of the decode gather, for verification."""
+    rows, width = indices.shape
+    device = indices.device
+    counts = torch.empty(rows, dtype=torch.int32, device=device)
+    cu = torch.arange(rows + 1, dtype=torch.int32, device=device) * width
+    packed_k = torch.empty(
+        (rows * width, *source.k_buffer.shape[1:]),
+        dtype=source.k_buffer.dtype,
+        device=device,
+    )
+    packed_v = torch.empty_like(packed_k)
+    qwen_sparse_valid_counts_triton(
+        source.sequence_lengths, indices, counts, rows, width
+    )
+    qwen_sparse_kv_extraction_compact_triton(
+        source.k_buffer,
+        source.v_buffer,
+        source.slot_table,
+        source.row_requests,
+        indices,
+        source.sequence_lengths,
+        cu,
+        packed_k,
+        packed_v,
+        rows,
+        width,
+        zero_fill_cols=width,
+    )
+    return counts, packed_k, packed_v
+
+
+def store_offloaded_kv(*, backend, layer, forward_batch, k, v) -> None:
+    """Store a forward's new K/V into the offload's device rows (decode: the
+    tail ring, extend: the scratch) and write it through to the host."""
+    offload = backend._kv_offload
+    mode = forward_batch.forward_mode
+    if mode.is_decode() or backend._is_speculative_paged_mode(mode):
+        metadata = backend._resolve_metadata(forward_batch)
+        rows = offload.new_token_rows(
+            row_seq_lens=metadata.sequence_lengths,
+            row_req=backend._row_requests(
+                forward_batch=forward_batch, metadata=metadata
+            ),
+        )
+    else:
+        rows = offload.extend_rows(forward_batch.out_cache_loc.numel())
+    pool = backend.token_to_kv_pool
+    layer_idx = pool.full_attention_layer_index(layer.layer_id)
+    if offload.verify:
+        if layer_idx == 0:
+            offload.snapshot_mapping()
+        backend.kv_layers.layer(layer.layer_id).store(
+            layer, forward_batch.out_cache_loc, k, v
+        )
+        offload.mirror(
+            layer_idx=layer_idx,
+            rows=rows,
+            loc=forward_batch.out_cache_loc,
+            pool_k=pool.full_kv_pool.k_buffer[layer_idx],
+            pool_v=pool.full_kv_pool.v_buffer[layer_idx],
+        )
+        return
+    backend.kv_layers.layer(layer.layer_id).store(layer, rows, k, v)
+    offload.write_through(
+        layer_idx=layer_idx, rows=rows, loc=forward_batch.out_cache_loc
+    )
+
+
+def gather_offloaded_context(
+    *,
+    backend,
+    layer,
+    forward_batch,
+    sequence_lens: torch.Tensor,
+    cu_seqlens_k: torch.Tensor,
+    total_k: int,
+    output_dtype: torch.dtype,
+) -> Tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]:
+    """Every context token of each request, in ``cu_seqlens_k`` order, read
+    from the host (the layout ``pack_qsa_prefill_kv`` builds from the pool)."""
+    device = sequence_lens.device
+    owner = torch.repeat_interleave(
+        torch.arange(sequence_lens.numel(), device=device),
+        sequence_lens.long(),
+        output_size=total_k,
+    )
+    positions = torch.arange(total_k, device=device) - cu_seqlens_k[:-1].long()[owner]
+    offload = backend._kv_offload
+    slots = offload.req_to_token[
+        forward_batch.req_pool_indices.long()[owner], positions
+    ]
+    pool = backend.token_to_kv_pool
+    layer_idx = pool.full_attention_layer_index(layer.layer_id)
+    k, v = offload.gather_context(layer_idx=layer_idx, slots=slots)
+    pool_k = pool.layer_router.read(layer.layer_id).key()
+    pool_v = pool.layer_router.read(layer.layer_id).value()
+    packed = (
+        k.view(pool_k.dtype).to(output_dtype),
+        v.view(pool_k.dtype).to(output_dtype),
+    )
+    if offload.verify:
+        expected = pack_qsa_prefill_kv(
+            k=pool_k,
+            v=pool_v,
+            req_to_token=offload.req_to_token,
+            req_indices=forward_batch.req_pool_indices,
+            cu_k=cu_seqlens_k,
+            total_k=total_k,
+            max_k=int(sequence_lens.max()),
+            output_dtype=output_dtype,
+        )
+        offload.check(
+            what="prefill context",
+            layer_idx=layer_idx,
+            actual=packed,
+            expected=expected,
+        )
+    return packed
+
+
+def forward_offloaded_attention(
+    *,
+    backend,
+    q: torch.Tensor,
+    layer,
+    forward_batch,
+    topk_indices: torch.Tensor,
+    trtllm_decode,
+) -> torch.Tensor:
+    """Decode / target verify over the offload's per-forward device-row table."""
+    pool = backend.token_to_kv_pool
+    offload = backend._kv_offload
+    layer_idx = pool.full_attention_layer_index(layer.layer_id)
+    metadata = backend._resolve_metadata(forward_batch)
+    positions = backend._expand_block_indices(topk_indices, metadata)
+    row_requests = backend._row_requests(forward_batch=forward_batch, metadata=metadata)
+    num_rows, width = positions.shape
+    rows_per_request = num_rows // forward_batch.batch_size
+    rows = offload.resolve_rows(
+        layer_idx=layer_idx,
+        positions=positions,
+        row_seq_lens=metadata.sequence_lengths,
+        row_req=row_requests,
+        rows_per_request=rows_per_request,
+    )
+    # Valid positions lead each row, so column ids keep the packing order.
+    columns = torch.arange(width, dtype=torch.int32, device=rows.device)
+    indices = torch.where(rows >= 0, columns, -1)
+    pool_k = pool.layer_router.read(layer.layer_id).key()
+    pool_v = pool.layer_router.read(layer.layer_id).value()
+    source = QSAKVGatherSource(
+        k_buffer=offload.dev_k[layer_idx].view(pool_k.dtype),
+        v_buffer=offload.dev_v[layer_idx].view(pool_v.dtype),
+        slot_table=rows,
+        row_requests=torch.arange(num_rows, device=rows.device),
+        sequence_lengths=torch.full(
+            (num_rows,), width, dtype=torch.int32, device=rows.device
+        ),
+    )
+    if offload.verify:
+        reference = QSAKVGatherSource(
+            k_buffer=pool_k,
+            v_buffer=pool_v,
+            slot_table=offload.req_to_token,
+            row_requests=row_requests,
+            sequence_lengths=metadata.sequence_lengths,
+        )
+        # CUDA-graph padding rows resolve to no device row by design.
+        real_rows = offload.real_rows(
+            num_rows=num_rows, rows_per_request=rows_per_request
+        )
+        reference_positions = torch.where(real_rows[:, None], positions, -1)
+        offload.check(
+            what="decode gather",
+            layer_idx=layer_idx,
+            actual=_pack_gathered_kv(source=source, indices=indices),
+            expected=_pack_gathered_kv(
+                source=reference,
+                indices=reference_positions.to(torch.int32).contiguous(),
+            ),
+        )
+    indices = indices.to(torch.int32).contiguous()
+    attention = (
+        backend._forward_varlen_sparse
+        if trtllm_decode is None
+        else partial(backend._forward_trtllm_sparse, trtllm_decode=trtllm_decode)
+    )
+    return attention(
+        q=q,
+        k_buffer=source.k_buffer,
+        v_buffer=source.v_buffer,
+        layer=layer,
+        forward_batch=forward_batch,
+        metadata=metadata,
+        topk_indices=indices,
+        source=source,
+    )

+"""Host offload of the QSA full-attention K/V with a per-request GPU hot cache.
+
+The full K/V of every QSA layer lives in pinned host memory, indexed by the
+logical KV slot (the allocator index stored in ``req_to_token``). The allocator,
+radix tree, chunked prefill and the compressed indexer keep addressing logical
+slots, so a radix prefix shared by several requests shares its host rows too.
+
+The GPU K/V pool of the QSA layers holds only device rows:
+
+* request slot ``r`` owns rows ``[r * region, (r + 1) * region)`` with
+  ``region = (hot_blocks + 2) * compress_ratio``: a two-block tail ring (block
+  ``b`` in ring slot ``b % 2``) for the newest tokens, then ``hot_blocks``
+  least-recently-used slots of one compressed block (``compress_ratio`` tokens)
+  each;
+* an extend scratch above the request regions.
+
+Every forward writes its new K/V to device rows and through to the host. A
+decode or target-verify forward maps each selected logical position to a device
+row, copying missing blocks from the host, and attention gathers through that
+row table instead of ``req_to_token``. A block copy is valid only while
+``req_to_token`` still maps its positions to the logical slots it was filled
+from; the radix cache rewrites a running request's mapping when it deduplicates
+an inserted prefix.
+"""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import logging
+import time
+from typing import List, Optional, Tuple
+
+import msgspec
+import torch
+
+from sglang.srt.environ import envs
+from sglang.srt.mem_cache.pool_host.common import (
+    HostTensorAllocator,
+    _cuda_host_unregister,
+    alloc_with_host_register,
+)
+from sglang.srt.utils import is_hip
+
+logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)
+
+# The block of a request's first new token and the next one: up to
+# ``compress_ratio`` new tokens span at most two blocks.
+TAIL_BLOCKS = 2
+GB = 1e9
+
+
+class QSAKVOffloadLayout(msgspec.Struct, frozen=True):
+    """Device-row layout of an offloaded QSA K/V pool."""
+
+    compress_ratio: int
+    hot_blocks: int
+    num_request_slots: int
+    scratch_rows: int
+    token_topk: int
+    rows_per_request: int
+
+    @property
+    def region_rows(self) -> int:
+        return (self.hot_blocks + TAIL_BLOCKS) * self.compress_ratio
+
+    @property
+    def tail_rows(self) -> int:
+        return TAIL_BLOCKS * self.compress_ratio
+
+    @property
+    def scratch_base(self) -> int:
+        return self.num_request_slots * self.region_rows
+
+    @property
+    def device_rows(self) -> int:
+        return self.scratch_base + self.scratch_rows
+
+
+def compute_offload_layout(
+    *,
+    compress_ratio: int,
+    token_topk: int,
+    hot_blocks: int,
+    num_request_slots: int,
+    rows_per_request: int,
+    max_extend_tokens: int,
+    page_size: int,
+) -> QSAKVOffloadLayout:
+    """Layout for ``num_request_slots`` request slots (``req_to_token`` rows).
+
+    ``rows_per_request`` is the query rows of one request in a forward (the
+    verify rows under speculative decoding, else 1); their selected blocks are
+    resolved together and must fit in the hot cache at once.
+    """
+    if page_size % compress_ratio:
+        raise ValueError(
+            f"QSA K/V offload needs a page size ({page_size}) that is a multiple "
+            f"of the compress ratio ({compress_ratio})"
+        )
+    if not 1 <= rows_per_request <= compress_ratio:
+        raise ValueError(
+            "QSA K/V offload supports at most compress_ratio "
+            f"({compress_ratio}) query rows per request, got {rows_per_request}"
+        )
+    needed = rows_per_request * (token_topk // compress_ratio)
+    if hot_blocks < needed:
+        raise ValueError(
+            f"--qsa-kv-offload-hot-blocks {hot_blocks} is below {needed}: "
+            f"{rows_per_request} query row(s) per request x "
+            f"{token_topk // compress_ratio} selected blocks must fit at once"
+        )
+    # Page-aligned so the device pool size is a whole number of pages.
+    scratch = max_extend_tokens + 2 * page_size
+    regions = num_request_slots * (hot_blocks + TAIL_BLOCKS) * compress_ratio
+    scratch += -(regions + scratch) % page_size

+        compress_ratio=compress_ratio,
+        hot_blocks=hot_blocks,
+        num_request_slots=num_request_slots,
+        scratch_rows=scratch,
+        token_topk=token_topk,
+        rows_per_request=rows_per_request,
+    )

+def offload_layout_from_config(
+    *, hf_config, num_request_slots: int, page_size: int

+        get_memory,
+        get_schedule,
+        max_speculative_num_draft_tokens,
+    )

+    profile = parse_qsa_profile(hf_config)
+    schedule = get_schedule()

+        compress_ratio=profile.compress_ratio,
+        token_topk=profile.budget,
+        hot_blocks=get_memory().qsa_kv_offload_hot_blocks,
+        num_request_slots=num_request_slots,
+        rows_per_request=max_speculative_num_draft_tokens() or 1,
+        max_extend_tokens=max(
+            schedule.chunked_prefill_size or 0, schedule.max_prefill_tokens or 0

+class QSAKVOffloadBudget(msgspec.Struct, frozen=True):
+    """GPU and host cost of the offload, for the KV pool sizing."""
+
+    # K/V bytes per logical token of the offloaded layers (all of them).
+    offloaded_bytes_per_token: int
+    # Device rows per request slot, and the scratch plus padding page.
+    region_rows: int
+    fixed_rows: int
+    # Hot-cache tables per request slot, all layers.
+    table_bytes_per_slot: int
+    host_size_gb: float
+    page_size: int
+    # Verify mode keeps the full GPU pool: the whole cell stays on the GPU.
+    verify: bool = False
+
+    def slot_bytes(self) -> int:
+        return self.region_rows * self.offloaded_bytes_per_token + (
+            self.table_bytes_per_slot
+        )
+
+    def gpu_cell(self, cell_bytes: int) -> int:
+        cell = cell_bytes - (0 if self.verify else self.offloaded_bytes_per_token)
+        if cell <= 0:
+            raise ValueError(f"QSA K/V offload: per-token GPU cost {cell} B")
+        return cell
+
+    def host_tokens(self) -> int:
+        if self.host_size_gb <= 0:
+            raise ValueError("--qsa-kv-offload-host-size must be positive")
+        host_rows = int(self.host_size_gb * GB) // self.offloaded_bytes_per_token
+        return host_rows - self.page_size
+
+    def max_total_tokens(
+        self, *, available_bytes: int, cell_bytes: int, num_request_slots: int
+    ) -> int:
+        """Logical KV pool size for ``num_request_slots`` request slots.
+
+        Per logical token the GPU keeps the cell minus the offloaded K/V (the
+        QSA index and any draft pool); each request slot costs its device rows
+        and tables. The host budget caps the pool at its K/V rows.
+        """
+        fixed = num_request_slots * self.slot_bytes() + (
+            self.fixed_rows * self.offloaded_bytes_per_token
+        )
+        if available_bytes <= fixed:
+            raise ValueError(
+                f"QSA K/V offload: the hot cache of {num_request_slots} request "
+                f"slots ({fixed / 2**30:.2f} GiB) exceeds the "
+                f"{available_bytes / 2**30:.2f} GiB KV budget; lower "
+                "--qsa-kv-offload-hot-blocks or --max-running-requests"
+            )
+        gpu_tokens = (available_bytes - fixed) // self.gpu_cell(cell_bytes)
+        tokens = min(gpu_tokens, self.host_tokens())
+        logger.info(
+            "QSA K/V offload sizing: %d request slots, hot cache %.2f GiB, GPU "
+            "allows %d tokens, host %.1f GB allows %d tokens",
+            num_request_slots,
+            fixed / 2**30,
+            gpu_tokens,
+            self.host_size_gb,
+            self.host_tokens(),
+        )
+        return tokens // self.page_size * self.page_size
+
+    def tokens_with_unused_slots(
+        self, *, max_total_tokens: int, cell_bytes: int, unused_slots: int
+    ) -> int:
+        """Pool size once ``unused_slots`` budgeted request slots are not built:
+        their GPU bytes hold logical tokens instead, up to the host budget."""
+        extra = unused_slots * self.slot_bytes() // self.gpu_cell(cell_bytes)
+        tokens = min(max_total_tokens + extra, self.host_tokens())
+        return tokens // self.page_size * self.page_size
+
+
+def offload_table_bytes_per_slot(
+    *, num_layers: int, hot_blocks: int, compress_ratio: int, context_len: int
+) -> int:
+    """Upper bound of the per-request-slot hot-cache tables of either resolve:
+    block->slot (int32 per block of the context), per-slot block, age, LRU
+    order, marks and source records, and the ring records."""
+    per_layer = (
+        (context_len // compress_ratio + 2 * TAIL_BLOCKS) * 4
+        + hot_blocks * (8 + 8 + 2 * 4 + 4 + 4 * compress_ratio)
+        + TAIL_BLOCKS * (8 + 4 * compress_ratio)
+        + 8
+    )
+    return num_layers * per_layer

+def _copy_rows(
+    *,
+    k_dst: torch.Tensor,
+    v_dst: torch.Tensor,
+    dst: torch.Tensor,
+    k_src: torch.Tensor,
+    v_src: torch.Tensor,
+    src: torch.Tensor,
+) -> None:
+    """K/V rows ``src[i]`` -> ``dst[i]`` between device and pinned host buffers."""
+    if dst.numel() == 0:
+        return
+    if dst.is_cuda:
+        from sglang.kernels.ops.kvcache.hicache import transfer_hicache_one_layer
+
+        transfer_hicache_one_layer(
+            k_cache_dst=k_dst,
+            v_cache_dst=v_dst,
+            indices_dst=dst,
+            k_cache_src=k_src,
+            v_cache_src=v_src,
+            indices_src=src,
+            element_dim=k_dst[0].numel(),

+    v_dst.index_copy_(0, dst, v_src.index_select(0, src))

+"""QSA K/V host offload on the GPU: pinned host store, JIT row copies and the
+decode gather.
+
+Each forward packs the selected K/V twice with the decode gather the QSA
+backend runs (``qwen_sparse_kv_extraction_compact_triton``): once from the full
+logical pool through ``req_to_token``, once from the offload's device rows
+through its per-forward row table. The packed scratch and valid counts must be
+bit-identical, under hot-cache eviction, radix remaps and chain verify.
+"""

+

+import torch
+

+from sglang.srt.layers.attention.qsa.kernel import expand_qsa_block_indices

+    qwen_sparse_kv_extraction_compact_triton,
+    qwen_sparse_valid_counts_triton,
+)
+from sglang.srt.mem_cache.qsa_kv_offload import (
+    QSAKVHostOffload,
+    compute_offload_layout,
+)

+TOPK = BLOCK_TOPK * CR + CR - 1
+

+    counts = torch.empty(rows, device="cuda", dtype=torch.int32)
+    ok = torch.empty(rows * STRIDE, HEADS, DIM, device="cuda", dtype=packed_dtype)
+    ov = torch.empty_like(ok)
+    cu = torch.arange(rows + 1, device="cuda", dtype=torch.int32) * STRIDE
+    qwen_sparse_valid_counts_triton(lens, indices, counts, rows, TOPK)
+    qwen_sparse_kv_extraction_compact_triton(
+        k, v, table, row_req, indices, lens, cu, ok, ov, rows, TOPK,
+        zero_fill_cols=STRIDE,
+    )  # fmt: skip
+    return counts, ok, ov
+

+@pytest.mark.parametrize("rows_per_request", [1, 4])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize(
+    "dtype,packed_dtype",
+    [
+        (torch.bfloat16, torch.bfloat16),
+        (torch.float8_e4m3fn, torch.bfloat16),
+        (torch.float8_e4m3fn, torch.float8_e4m3fn),
+    ],
+)

+    layout = compute_offload_layout(

+        hot_blocks=q * BLOCK_TOPK,
+        num_request_slots=requests + 1,
+        rows_per_request=q,
+        max_extend_tokens=4096,
+        page_size=64,

+"""QSA backend with the K/V host offload vs. the full GPU K/V pool.
+
+Two QSA pools receive the same K/V: one keeps it on the GPU (upstream), the other
+offloads it to pinned host memory (``kv_offload_layout``). The QSA backend runs
+the same forwards on both: three prefill chunks per request (the later chunks
+gather their cached context from the host) and decode steps whose selections
+evict and reload hot-cache blocks and cross the tail ring. The attention outputs
+must be bit-identical. Breaking the scratch or ring rows the backend stores to,
+the host write-through, the prefill context gather or the decode row table
+turns this red.
+"""
+

+from types import SimpleNamespace
+
+import pytest
+import torch
+
+from sglang.srt.environ import envs

+TOKEN_TOPK = 2048
